config.classes_note: Five classes, each the census's own kind or intersection for the entity, stated by field sources at the loci given: (1) task benchmarks of AI capability on occupational and economically valuable work (census kind 'benchmark', evidence_kind 'task benchmark'; B3 Abstract, B4, B8 §1, B2, B7); (2) one-shot, precisely specified commissioned tasks (B8 §5 Limitations, §2.3; the LV record's lv_intersection 'a fixed commission' and intersection labor-with-ai 'task fidelity'), the class on which the archive's DSL (#771) states its identification condition; (3) the user's review and redo of model output (B8 §3.2, A.2.1; intersection labor-with-ai 'correction burdens and user labor drag'), the class of #771's User Labor Drag; (4) expert labor producing AI evaluation, the professionals as task writers, reviewers and graders (B8 §2.2, §2.5, A.5.2; B10; intersection labor-producing-ai 'annotation, moderation, evaluation'); (5) model graders and their self-preference (B8 A.6.2; B2; B7; census negative_tags). The archive's instruments of labor direction (DSL and the DS-6 directionality stack, #771; its canonical definition surface on laborvector.org, #1392; User Labor Drag, #771 §8) bear on classes (2) and (3) at the loci given in reading.json; the semantic-labor line bears on (4) only where a sentence says something of the labor that produces evaluations or training data as a class. The aliases are the entity's name (GDPval; 'GDP-val' and case variants matched) and its arXiv number. 'GDPval-AA' (Artificial Analysis's evaluation framework on OpenAI's GDPval dataset) is a distinct entity the alias pattern also matches; a sentence naming it is read for what it says of GDPval. Admission by reading (§3.4): D where a deposit names the entity and says something of it; O-class where a sentence applies an archive category (DSL, task-origin, user labor drag, the directionality stack, semantic labor, provenance erasure) to one of the classes; a bare list, a citation-list entry or a reference line is not a claim.
